Notes: Dhakal p. 61 prints /kin.la.rə/ “buy.PROS”; p. 56 identifies -larʰə as the prospective marker. The root kin- matches Turner3594, which gives Nepali kinnu “to buy,” Maithili kinab and Bhojpuri kinal. The prospective suffix is Darai morphology, not part of the etymon. Dhakal p. 61 prints /kan.cʰə/ “the youngest one.” Turner2735 gives Nepali kāncho “younger, the youngest brother,” and its addenda Jaunsari kaṇchā “younger, youngest.” This is the affricate branch of kanyasa-, not the separate kaniṣṭhá article 2718. Darai pp. 61-62; source PDF and full CDIAL reviewed; no rebuild

Dhakal p. 62 prints /əl.cʰi/ “lazy.” Turner1371 lists adjective descendants of ālasya, including Nepali alchi “lazy,” alongside Punjabi ālsī and Oriya āḷasi. The Darai affricate adjective matches the Nepali form closely. Darai pp. 61-62; source PDF and full CDIAL reviewed; no rebuild
